content: {"summary":"Node 02 ran out of /var space in November 2025 because an OpenSearch log file was not rotated and grew about 1 GB per day, filling the root disk. The remediation follows runbook RB‑008: locate the large log, restore the missing logrotate configuration (using copytruncate), run logrotate forcefully, and clean any journal files.","likely_cause":"Unrotated OpenSearch log file under /var/log/opensearch grew unchecked and exhausted disk space.","confidence":"high","claims":[{"text":"Disk filled because an unrotated OpenSearch log grew ~1 GB per day, accumulating ~29 GB.","evidence_ids":["INC-0101#1","RB-008#1"],"quote":"The log grows about 1 GB a day."},{"text":"Cleaning follows runbook RB‑008: add missing logrotate for /var/log/opensearch/*.log with copytruncate and run logrotate -f.","evidence_ids":["RB-008#1"],"quote":"run `sudo logrotate -f /etc/logrotate.d/<name>`"}],"next_checks":["Verify that /etc/logrotate.d contains a config for opensearch logs on all search‑cluster nodes","Confirm the logrotate file uses copytruncate and is applied via config management","Check for any processes still holding deleted log files with `lsof +L1`","Monitor /var usage after cleanup to ensure it stays below 80%"]}
